Blockchain can provide a common record of capability commitments, session grants, revocations, and audit anchors among parties that do not fully trust a single operator, but enforcing every A2A message, tool call, or artifact on-chain would add substantial latency and cost. This paper proposes SC-A2A Gateway, a blockchain-powered gateway with smart contracts for policy enforcement and audit in A2A collaboration. SC-A2A uses smart contracts to verify capability status, runtime and schema commitments, tool-scope commitments, delegation constraints, and revocation state when a session grant or delegated grant is created, while gateways enforce data and tool policies off-chain during execution. Raw prompts, personal data, tool parameters, and artifacts remain off-chain; only hashes, grant state, revocation records, and audit roots are stored on-chain. We evaluate a prototype using a procurement scenario, official A2A v1 Node.js and Python SDKs, an LLM/MCP workflow, and a custom Hyperledger Besu QBFT network. The results show that SC-A2A blocks the tested policy violations, completes concurrent A2A multi-agent workflows without per-message blockchain transactions, and exposes a configurable trade-off between revocation freshness and blockchain-state reads.
